entrypoints.summary: The public changeOwner(v,r,s,hash,newOwner) function accepts caller-supplied ECDSA recovery inputs and a proposed recipient.
The organizer trigger obtains an instance RPC endpoint and submits changeOwner with constructed recovery values and the attacker wallet as newOwner.

affected_components.role: Public ownership-transfer verifier, owner-gated state transition, and solved-state reader.

code_slices.surrounding_context: solve is restricted by onlyOwner and changes solved to true; isSolved returns the resulting state.
code_slices.vulnerable: changeOwner recovers signer from caller-supplied hash and signature values, requires signer == owner(), then transfers ownership to caller-supplied newOwner.

observability.channel: on-chain RPC and challenge TCP service
negative_controls: A transfer attempt whose recovered signer is not the current owner reverts at the signer equality requirement.
The source contains no observed execution result for either control.
observability.positive_marker: isSolved returns true and the trigger then requests token redemption.

preconditions: Access to the challenge service and completion of its proof of work.
Availability of the instance RPC endpoint, attacker funded key, token, and Recovery contract address.
A challenge-instance transaction from which the trigger can recover the current owner public key.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Service interaction followed by RPC block and transaction lookup.
trigger_steps.summary: Obtain instance connection material after proof of work and recover the owner public key from the selected chain transaction.
Construct v, r, s, and hash that recover the owner public key, then call changeOwner with the attacker wallet as newOwner.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Owner-gated solve transaction followed by isSolved RPC call and token submission.
trigger_steps.summary: Call solve from the attacker wallet and inspect the solved state before redeeming the token.

relation_candidates.rationale: Binding the signed authorization to the intended recipient and execution context would remove acceptance of arbitrary raw recovery inputs as sufficient transfer authority.
The trigger reads the solved state after solve and subsequently redeems the service token.

impact.affected_asset: Recovery contract ownership and its solved state.
impact.attacker_capability: A contract user can become owner by supplying recovery values accepted for the current owner without presenting an authorization message bound to the requested recipient.
impact.security_effect: Unauthorized ownership transfer followed by completion of the owner-only solved state.

causal_trace.summary: The ownership-change entrypoint accepts an arbitrary hash, raw v/r/s values, and newOwner from any caller; it only rejects the zero recipient before recovery.

Authorization is treated as satisfied solely when ecrecover over attacker-selected recovery inputs equals the current owner; the verifier does not construct or verify a contract-defined message that binds newOwner to the ownership change.

The official trigger recovers a public key from an on-chain transaction, constructs values that locally recover that key from its selected message hash, and supplies those values to changeOwner; on the owner-address equality check, the contract executes _transferOwnership(newOwner).
After ownership is transferred to the attacker wallet, the trigger invokes the owner-gated solve function, which sets solved to true; it then reads isSolved and redeems the challenge token.

failure.operation: _transferOwnership(newOwner) after an owner-address match from ecrecover(hash,v,r,s)

primary_invariant.statement: An ownership transfer must require authorization by the current owner for the specific proposed new owner and transfer context, rather than only recovery of the owner address from caller-controlled raw ECDSA inputs.
primary_invariant.violated_because: changeOwner passes caller-provided hash and signature components directly to ecrecover, compares the recovered address to owner(), and then transfers ownership to the independently supplied newOwner.

quality.review_notes: The contract source and organizer-supplied trigger establish the mechanism and intended state oracle. No execution transcript is supplied, so this record does not assert that the trigger was run successfully. The trigger assumes a challenge-specific latest-block transaction layout. No invariant-restoring patch or maintainer remediation is present; mitigation classes are inferred from the demonstrated verifier defect, not sourced as an applied fix.

remediation.invariant_restored: Only an authorization that the contract verifies as covering the intended new owner and the relevant execution domain/state can authorize ownership transfer; raw recovery outputs alone are insufficient.
mitigation_classes: contract-defined ownership-transfer authorization bound to the recipient
domain-separated signature authorization with anti-replay state

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The organizer trigger completes proof of work, receives a per-instance RPC endpoint and funded key, reads an on-chain transaction to recover the owner public key, and derives recovery-compatible inputs before submitting changeOwner.
data_structure_invariants: owner must not be transferred based solely on a recovered address from caller-controlled raw inputs.
solved may be set only by the current owner through solve.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: The caller chooses all recovery values and newOwner; acceptance requires ecrecover(hash,v,r,s) to equal the current owner.
numeric_domains.name: ECDSA recovery inputs

state_context.state_machine: Initial owner controls solve; a public caller can invoke changeOwner; accepted recovery values move ownership to newOwner; the new owner can invoke solve to set solved true.

oracle.expected_negative: A correctly bound ownership-transfer authorization should reject recovery values that are not an authorization for the supplied newOwner, preventing the attacker wallet from satisfying onlyOwner on solve.
oracle.expected_positive: A reproduction submits the constructed changeOwner values, observes the attacker wallet can invoke solve, and reads isSolved as true before challenge-token redemption.
